title: Billing Dispute Resolution Policy
content: When a customer reports a duplicate or erroneous charge, agents must initiate a billing dispute within 24 hours of the report. Verify the charge in the billing system by navigating to Account > Transactions and filtering by date range. Duplicate charges are defined as two identical transactions processed within 72 hours with the same amount and merchant reference. For confirmed duplicates, issue a full refund to the original payment method within 3-5 business days. Premium account holders are entitled to an expedited 24-hour refund processing SLA. Document the dispute in the CRM under case type 'Billing Dispute' and attach screenshots of the duplicate transaction evidence. Notify the customer via email once the refund is initiated, including a reference number and the expected credit date. If the duplicate was caused by a known system error, apply the standard goodwill credit of $10 in addition to the refund.

title: Refund Processing Procedures
content: Refunds are processed through the payment gateway integration in the admin portal. Standard refund timeline: 3-5 business days for credit cards, 5-7 business days for debit cards, 1-2 business days for store credit. To initiate a refund, locate the original transaction ID in Billing > Transaction History, click 'Issue Refund', select the refund amount (full or partial), and confirm. Partial refunds may be issued for service disruptions or billing errors that affected only a portion of the service period. For amounts over $500, a supervisor approval is required before the refund can be processed. Premium account refunds bypass the standard queue and are processed with priority handling. Always confirm the refund in writing to the customer's registered email address. Keep the original transaction ID in the case notes for audit purposes.

title: Double Charge Known Issue — Payment Gateway Batch Processing
content: A known intermittent issue in the payment gateway batch processor (incident INC-2847) can cause duplicate charges during the nightly settlement window between 02:00 and 04:00 UTC. Affected charges will have identical amounts and timestamps within a 2-minute window. This issue has been confirmed by the engineering team and a fix is scheduled for the next release cycle. If a customer reports a double charge and the timestamps fall within the 02:00-04:00 UTC window, this is a confirmed system error. In these cases, agents should: (1) Apologize and acknowledge the system error without requiring the customer to provide further evidence, (2) Issue the refund immediately without supervisor approval regardless of amount, (3) Apply the $10 goodwill credit automatically, (4) Escalate to engineering via the INC-2847 tracking channel for monitoring. Do not ask the customer to wait for investigation — this is a known and confirmed issue.

title: Account Types, Tiers, and SLA Entitlements
content: The platform supports three account tiers: Standard, Professional, and Premium. Standard accounts receive email support with a 48-hour SLA. Professional accounts receive email and chat support with a 12-hour SLA. Premium accounts receive email, chat, and phone support with a 4-hour SLA for critical issues and a 24-hour SLA for general inquiries. Premium accounts also receive priority refund processing (24-hour vs. standard 3-5 business days), a dedicated account manager for accounts with MRR over $500, and a 99.9% uptime SLA with financial compensation for downtime exceeding the threshold. When a customer contacts support, verify their account tier in the CRM before quoting resolution timelines. Misquoting SLAs to a Premium customer is a compliance issue and must be corrected immediately if caught.

title: Customer Account Lookup and Verification Guide
content: Before taking any action on an account, agents must verify customer identity using at least two of the following: registered email address, last four digits of payment method on file, account creation date, or the last transaction amount. Navigate to CRM > Accounts > Search and enter the customer's email or account ID. The account detail page shows tier, payment methods, open cases, and transaction history. For billing-related cases, always cross-reference the transaction history in the billing system (Billing > Accounts > [Account ID]) to confirm the details match what the customer is reporting. If identity cannot be verified, do not discuss account details or process any changes. Escalate to a senior agent if the customer disputes the verification outcome.

title: Escalation Procedures and Tier-2 Handoff
content: Escalate a case to Tier-2 support when any of the following conditions are met: the customer requests to speak with a supervisor, the issue cannot be resolved within two agent interactions, the case involves a charge over $1000, a data privacy concern is raised, or the customer has a history of three or more unresolved cases in the past 90 days. To escalate, use the CRM 'Escalate' button, select the escalation tier and reason from the dropdown, add a case summary of at least 50 words, and confirm the handoff. The Tier-2 team has a 2-hour SLA for Premium customers and a 24-hour SLA for Standard customers. Inform the customer of the escalation and provide the new case reference number. Never promise a specific resolution outcome during escalation — only promise timely follow-up.

title: FAQ: How Long Does a Refund Take?
content: Customers frequently ask about refund timelines. Standard response: refunds to credit cards take 3-5 business days to appear on the statement, and refunds to debit cards take 5-7 business days. The delay is due to bank processing cycles outside of our control. Once we initiate a refund, we send a confirmation email with the expected credit date. If the refund has not appeared after 7 business days, advise the customer to contact their bank with the refund reference number we provided. Store credit refunds are applied instantly and visible in the account portal. Premium accounts receive expedited processing and refunds typically appear within 1-2 business days. Seasonal bank delays (holidays, end of month) can extend these windows by 1-2 additional business days.

title: FAQ: What Is the Dispute Process for Unauthorized Charges?
content: If a customer believes a charge was unauthorized (not a duplicate, but fraud or error), the process differs from a standard billing dispute. The customer must complete the Unauthorized Charge Declaration form, available in their account portal under Security > Disputes. Upon submission, the account is flagged for fraud review, the charge is provisionally reversed within 24 hours, and the fraud team initiates a 10-business-day investigation. If fraud is confirmed, the reversal becomes permanent and the customer is issued a new payment method token. If the charge is found to be legitimate (e.g., a forgotten subscription), the reversal is cancelled and the customer is notified with evidence. Agents should not process unauthorized charge cases as standard billing disputes — route them through the fraud declaration workflow.

title: Premium Subscription Features and Benefits
content: The Premium subscription tier provides access to all platform features including advanced analytics, API access with rate limits of 10,000 requests per day, priority customer support, dedicated account management for qualifying accounts, and monthly billing reports. Premium subscribers also receive early access to beta features, a 30-day data retention extension beyond the standard policy, and integration support for up to three third-party tools. The monthly cost is $149.99, billed on the same calendar day as the original subscription activation. Annual billing is available at a 15% discount. Downgrading from Premium to a lower tier requires 30 days notice and takes effect at the start of the next billing cycle. Features included at the Premium tier are documented in the Premium Features Matrix (see Appendix B of the Product Documentation).

title: Goodwill Credits and Compensation Policy
content: Agents are authorized to issue goodwill credits up to $25 per case without supervisor approval. Credits between $25 and $100 require supervisor approval via the CRM approval workflow. Credits over $100 require Tier-2 or manager sign-off. Goodwill credits are applied as account balance and deducted from the next billing cycle. They do not expire within the current contract year. Situations warranting goodwill credits include: confirmed system errors causing customer inconvenience, repeated support interactions for the same unresolved issue, service outages affecting the customer's workflow, and any case where the customer has expressed significant dissatisfaction and a credit would reasonably restore goodwill. Document the business justification for every goodwill credit in the case notes. Credits must not be used as incentives to close a case without resolution.

title: Chargeback Prevention and Customer Communication
content: A chargeback occurs when a customer disputes a charge directly with their bank rather than with support. Chargebacks are costly (typically $15-$25 in bank fees per incident) and can affect merchant account standing. To prevent chargebacks, agents should resolve billing disputes proactively within the first contact where possible. If a customer mentions they are considering a chargeback, escalate immediately and offer expedited resolution. Document any customer statement about initiating a chargeback as a flag in the CRM. For Premium customers, a chargeback threat should trigger immediate Tier-2 escalation. After a chargeback is filed by a bank, the standard support resolution path is suspended — the case is handled by the Finance team. Agents should not contact customers about cases with active bank chargebacks without Finance approval.

title: HR Policy: Remote Work Expense Reimbursement
content: Employees working remotely are eligible for reimbursement of home office expenses up to $500 per calendar year. Eligible expenses include ergonomic furniture (chair, desk, monitor stand), high-speed internet service (up to $50 per month), and peripherals (keyboard, mouse, headset). Expenses must be submitted through the HR portal within 60 days of purchase. Reimbursements are processed in the next payroll cycle after approval. Receipts are required for all expenses over $25. Home office expenses are considered taxable benefits in some jurisdictions — employees should consult the tax guidance document in the HR knowledge base. Approval is granted by the direct manager. Recurring expenses (internet) are auto-approved upon initial setup. One-time purchases over $200 require a brief written justification.

title: Employee Onboarding Checklist — Week 1
content: Welcome to the team. During your first week, complete the following: (1) Set up your company email and Slack workspace. (2) Complete mandatory security training in the LMS (HR > Learning > Onboarding). (3) Schedule a 30-minute intro call with your manager. (4) Request system access for all required tools by submitting an IT ticket. (5) Review the company handbook in the HR portal. (6) Complete payroll setup including direct deposit and tax withholding forms. (7) Attend the weekly all-hands meeting on Friday at 10:00 AM. (8) Review your 90-day onboarding plan in the HR portal under My Plan. Your buddy will be in touch within 24 hours of your start date. For questions about any of these steps, contact HR at hr@company.com or your assigned HR business partner.

title: Tech Support: WiFi and Network Connectivity Issues
content: For customers reporting connectivity issues with the platform, begin with standard network diagnostics. Ask the customer to run a speed test at speedtest.net and confirm they have at least 5 Mbps download and 2 Mbps upload. Common causes of connectivity issues include VPN interference, corporate firewall rules blocking WebSocket connections, and outdated browser versions. Advise the customer to whitelist the following domains: api.platform.com, ws.platform.com, cdn.platform.com. If the issue persists, collect a HAR file export from the browser developer tools and attach it to the support case. For mobile app connectivity, advise clearing the app cache and reinstalling if necessary. Escalate to the infrastructure team if the issue appears to be on the platform side (check the status page at status.platform.com before assuming customer-side fault).

title: Legal Disclaimer: Terms of Service Summary for Agent Reference
content: Agents must not make legally binding commitments on behalf of the company beyond what is explicitly authorized in the policies and procedures documentation. Do not quote specific legal statutes or interpret contract terms for customers — direct them to legal@company.com or the Terms of Service document at platform.com/terms. Refunds are governed by the Refund Policy in the Terms of Service (Section 8). The company reserves the right to modify pricing with 30 days notice. Dispute resolution is governed by binding arbitration as described in Section 14. Agents should not confirm or deny ongoing litigation. Any customer correspondence that references legal action should be forwarded to the Legal team immediately via the CRM legal flag. This summary is for internal reference only and must not be shared verbatim with customers.

title: API Rate Limits and Quota Management
content: The platform API enforces rate limits per account tier to ensure fair usage. Standard accounts: 1,000 requests per day, 100 per minute. Professional accounts: 5,000 requests per day, 500 per minute. Premium accounts: 10,000 requests per day, 1,000 per minute. Rate limit headers are returned with every API response: X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset. When the limit is reached, the API returns HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header. Burst capacity is available for Premium accounts: up to 2x the per-minute limit for bursts not exceeding 10 seconds. To request a custom rate limit increase, submit a request to enterprise@platform.com with use case justification and expected volume. Rate limit violations are logged and accounts with repeated violations may be subject to temporary throttling.

title: FAQ: How to Update Payment Method on File
content: Customers can update their payment method at any time from the Account Settings > Billing section. Click 'Add Payment Method', enter the new card details, and set it as the default. The old payment method remains on file until deleted. If a customer needs to update their payment method because of a compromised card, advise them to also check for any recent unauthorized charges and report them through the Security > Disputes workflow. After updating the payment method, the next billing cycle will use the new card. Mid-cycle updates do not trigger an immediate charge. If a payment has failed due to an expired card, updating the card and clicking 'Retry Payment' will reattempt the charge. Note: payment method updates require the account owner to be logged in — agents cannot update payment methods on behalf of customers for security reasons.

title: Office Space Booking Policy
content: Employees wishing to use the headquarters office space must book a desk in advance using the Office Booking portal at office.internal.company.com. Hot desks are available on a first-come, first-served basis and can be reserved up to 2 weeks in advance. Meeting rooms must be booked at least 1 hour before use. Recurring room bookings are not allowed — each occurrence must be booked individually. Visitors must be pre-registered at least 24 hours before arrival by completing the Visitor Registration form in the portal. Parking is available in Lot B and Lot C; Lot A is reserved for executives. Kitchen facilities are on floors 3 and 7. For building access issues, contact facilities@company.com. The office is open Monday through Friday, 7:00 AM to 8:00 PM. Weekend access requires prior approval from your department head.

title: Subscription Cancellation and Proration Policy
content: Customers may cancel their subscription at any time. Cancellations take effect at the end of the current billing period — access is maintained until that date. No refunds are issued for unused portions of the current billing period under the standard policy. However, if the customer has been charged for a period during which a service outage exceeded the SLA threshold (99.9% uptime for Premium), a prorated refund for the outage period may be issued upon request. To process a cancellation, navigate to Account > Subscription > Cancel and select the cancellation reason. Send the customer a confirmation email with the effective date. If the customer cancels within 3 days of a renewal charge, evaluate whether a full refund of the renewal charge is warranted under the goodwill credit policy. Reactivation within 30 days of cancellation preserves account data.
